description: cost-ledger (ADR 0031, ADR 0025): the golden rows of the `llm_call` ledger, which migration 0082 creates. `fields` is the table's columns, one entry per column, and each tier's suite holds it to the table both ways: core to the Drizzle table that generates the migration, the worker to the columns the migrated database has. A column added to the table and not here, or here and not to the table, is that tier's red suite. Every row carries exactly those keys and no others, which is how *never the prompt or the completion* is checked against the disk rather than left to a reader: a row cannot carry what the field set does not name, and the field set names nothing that could hold either. `outcomes` is the words `outcome` takes, which the table's check constraint lists, and each is behind at least one row so neither is a word with nothing under it. `purpose` is held to each tier's vocabulary: the api's `LLM_PURPOSES` over the schema's `llm_purpose` enum (packages/core/src/llm/index.ts, packages/schema/src/llm-tables.ts), and in the worker the purpose it seeds a model choice with and resolves one by, `model_choice_for(purpose)` casting to that same enum. Neither suite reads the other tier's list. A row names the run or the answer it served under two nullable columns with exactly one of them set, because a run and an answer are separate records; `answer_id` is a question's record. `id` and `called_at` are the row's own: `called_at` is what the spending limit sums a calendar month by. `cost_gbp` carries its unit in its name and its value as a decimal string: money is not a float, and the column is `numeric`. It is pounds sterling, priced at the rates set in pounds for the call's day; a provider's dollar list price is converted by the person who sets the price, on the day they set it, so no exchange rate is read when a call is made (owner, 14/10/2026). `seconds` is wall-clock, ADR 0025's own word for it. The rows are six across two workspaces: one per purpose, and one whose outcome is a failure. Two carry `tokens_out` 0 — the embedding call, which has no output tokens at all, and the failed answering call, which produced none — so no reader can take a zero for a failure, the outcome word being the only thing that says so, and the failed row still carries a cost because the tokens it sent were spent. The figures are one plausible day's calls and no suite asserts a number among them. ADR 0025's retention, six months of rows then a monthly per-workspace aggregate, is not built yet.

fields.is: the workspace whose spend this call is, and the column every signal over this ledger groups by
the row's own id, unique within its workspace
when the call was made, the instant the spending limit counts its month by
what the call was for, from the vocabulary both tiers hold these rows to
the `model_choice` row the call was resolved through, so spend can be read back per model choice
the model actually called, beside the model choice because a model choice's model is edited and a row is not
tokens sent, which are spent whatever the call returns
tokens returned, zero where a call returns none and zero where it fails
wall-clock time the call took, the figure the onboarding ETA is read off
what the call cost in pounds sterling at the price set for its day, a decimal string because money is not a float
the run this call served, null where it served an answer
the answer this call served, null where it served a run

outcomes.is: the call returned, and its tokens, seconds and cost are what it spent doing so
the call returned nothing the caller could use — refused, cut off or timed out — and what it spent before that is still spent
